condition.keyFindings: The dominant conspicuous finding is DENSE CHALK-WHITE CALCIFICATION INSIDE the intervertebral discs at five consecutive lumbar levels. Each narrowed disc space contains a broad bright mineralised horizontal band occupying its central substance, clearly brighter than both adjacent vertebral bodies. The calcified disc bands are separate from the thin vertebral cortical endplates. The vertebral bodies themselves retain grey trabecular interiors, normal height and smooth cortical outlines. This is the classic dense multilevel intradiscal calcification pattern of ochronotic spondylosis.
